meta.preparedDetail: Prepared Fri Nov 13, 2026, about 8:00 a.m. ET, before the U.S. open

top50.title: The 50 Largest U.S. Companies by Market Cap
top50.universeNote: U.S.-headquartered, U.S.-listed companies only. Foreign ADRs excluded. Linde excluded from this list. SpaceX included; it is not in the S&P 500. Alphabet and Berkshire counted once, all share classes combined.

top3.title: Largest S&P 500 Companies by Sector
top3.universeNote: Three largest S&P 500 members in each of the 11 GICS sectors. The report cites Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies, cross-checked with StockAnalysis (SPY holdings), for membership and GICS sectors. Linde is included as an S&P 500 Materials member.

correlation.method: Pearson correlation of daily returns vs SPY and QQQ
correlation.priceSource: Yahoo Finance, as stated in the report
correlation.windowDetail: 1-year daily returns. SpaceX uses 106 trading days from Jun 15, 2026.
correlation.bands: Absolute value: H >= 0.50, M 0.25-0.49, L below 0.25

companies.name: Apple
companies.blurb: Makes the iPhone, Mac, and iPad, and runs the App Store and iCloud.
companies.warNote: Greater China (mainland, Hong Kong, Taiwan) was $82.4B, or 17% of FY2026 sales ($478.8B). Substantially all hardware is made by partners primarily in mainland China, Taiwan, India, Japan, South Korea, and Vietnam.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.blurb: Designs the chips that power AI data centers and many gaming PCs.
companies.warNote: Wafers come mainly from TSMC (and Samsung). FY2026 revenue: China incl. Hong Kong $19.7B (9%) and Taiwan-headquartered customers $42.3B (20%) of $215.9B.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.blurb: Sells Windows, Office, and Azure cloud computing to businesses and consumers.
companies.warNote: FY2026 revenue was 51% U.S. ($170.8B) and 49% other countries ($161.0B); China is not broken out. Rating is Medium because nearly half of sales are abroad, not because a China share is disclosed.

companies.name: Alphabet
companies.blurb: Owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, and Google Cloud.
companies.warNote: FY2025 revenue was 48% U.S., 29% EMEA, 17% Asia-Pacific, 6% other Americas. China is not a disclosed market; core consumer services are largely unavailable there. All share classes counted once.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.blurb: Runs the main online store, Prime, and Amazon Web Services cloud.
companies.warNote: FY2025 sales: North America $426.3B (59%), International $161.9B (23%), AWS $128.7B (18%). China is not broken out.

companies.name: SpaceX
companies.blurb: Builds reusable rockets and the Starlink satellite internet network.
companies.warNote: Q3 2026 10-Q: Starlink serves consumer, enterprise, and government customers. No 10-K yet (listed June 2026); China sales are not a disclosed line. Rating is qualitative, based on U.S. launch and government connectivity. Correlation uses 106 trading days from Jun 15, 2026.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.blurb: Makes networking and smartphone chips, plus enterprise software (VMware).
companies.warNote: Most front-end wafers are outsourced, including to TSMC. China incl. Hong Kong was $11.2B, or 17%, of FY2025 revenue ($63.9B).

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.blurb: Runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and the Quest headset business.
companies.warNote: FY2025 revenue: U.S. $74.8B of $201.0B; Asia-Pacific $53.8B (27%). China is not a disclosed segment; Facebook and Instagram are not generally available there.

companies.name: Tesla
companies.blurb: Builds electric cars, energy storage, and some solar products.
companies.warNote: China was $21.0B, or 22%, of FY2025 revenue ($94.8B), and Tesla builds cars in Shanghai.

companies.name: Eli Lilly
companies.blurb: Makes prescription drugs, including widely used diabetes and weight-loss medicines.
companies.warNote: China was $1.95B, or 3%, of FY2025 revenue ($65.2B).

companies.name: Berkshire Hathaway
companies.blurb: A holding company for insurance (GEICO), the BNSF railroad, utilities, and a large stock portfolio.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K has no material China revenue line. Operations are mainly U.S. insurance, rail, and energy. Portfolio holdings (including Apple) are indirect and are not treated as the company's own China sales. Combined Class A and B.

companies.name: Walmart
companies.blurb: The largest U.S. retailer, including Sam's Club and a growing online business.
companies.warNote: Walmart U.S. was 68% of FY2026 sales; International was $130.4B (19%) across 18 countries including China. China is not broken out as a material stand-alone line.

companies.name: AMD
companies.blurb: Designs PC, game-console, and data-center chips that compete with Intel and NVIDIA.
companies.warNote: Leading-edge chips rely primarily on TSMC. China incl. Hong Kong was $7.8B (22%) and Taiwan $5.2B (15%) of FY2025 sales ($34.6B).

companies.name: JPMorgan Chase
companies.blurb: The largest U.S. bank, with consumer banking, credit cards, and a global investment bank.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K does not break out a material China revenue share. The only Taiwan mention in the extract is about fund share classes, not operations.

companies.name: Micron Technology
companies.blurb: Makes memory chips used in phones, PCs, and AI servers.
companies.warNote: FY2026 (year ended Sep 3, 2026): Taiwan held $27.6B of $64.0B in long-lived assets (43%). China sales have also been limited by a 2023 CAC ban on critical-infrastructure purchases.

companies.name: Visa
companies.blurb: Runs the Visa card network that banks use to process payments worldwide.
companies.warNote: U.S. was about 38% of FY2026 net revenue; no other country was 10% or more. The 10-K names UnionPay as the leading network in China.

companies.name: Exxon Mobil
companies.blurb: An integrated oil and gas company: it finds, produces, refines, and sells fuel.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K shows material Asia production (consolidated crude 445 kbd) and a global shipping/marketing system. The filing does not name the Strait of Hormuz.

companies.name: Johnson & Johnson
companies.blurb: Makes prescription drugs and medical devices (Band-Aid to surgical tools).
companies.warNote: About 43% of FY2025 sales were outside the U.S., including 15% in Asia-Pacific and Africa. China is not broken out.

companies.name: Mastercard
companies.blurb: Runs a global card-payment network, similar to Visa.
companies.warNote: U.S. was about 29% of FY2025 net revenue; no other country was more than 10%.

companies.name: AbbVie
companies.blurb: A drugmaker known for immunology and other specialty medicines.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K does not present China as a 10%+ market. Midgard's compiled 10-K table shows about 2% China; that percentage is unverified here (single compiled source).

companies.name: Costco
companies.blurb: A membership warehouse club selling food and household goods in bulk.
companies.warNote: Operates warehouses in the U.S. and many other countries, including Taiwan and China, but the U.S. is the core of the business. China/Taiwan sales are not broken out.

companies.name: Chevron
companies.blurb: An integrated oil and gas company with large production and refining operations.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K reports substantial proved reserves and production in Asia and other international areas. The filing does not name the Strait of Hormuz.

companies.name: Coca-Cola
companies.blurb: Sells Coca-Cola and other drinks through bottlers around the world.
companies.warNote: Swire Coca-Cola, a major bottler, operates in 11 mainland China provinces, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. Coca-Cola does not break out a China revenue percentage.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.blurb: Sells data and AI software used by governments and large companies.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K describes software platforms sold to government and commercial customers, including U.S. government work. China is not a disclosed revenue line.

companies.name: Cisco
companies.blurb: Makes the networking gear that companies and carriers use to move data.
companies.warNote: Business is managed in three regions, including Asia Pacific, Japan, and China (APJC). The 10-K cites China-Taiwan relations as a geopolitical risk and notes price-focused Asian competition.

companies.name: Oracle
companies.blurb: Sells business software and cloud databases used by large companies.
companies.warNote: Asia Pacific was $7.6B, or 11%, of FY2026 revenue ($67.4B). The 10-K cites China-Taiwan tensions as a supply-chain risk.

companies.name: Procter & Gamble
companies.blurb: Makes household brands such as Tide, Pampers, Gillette, and Crest.
companies.warNote: Operations outside the U.S. generate more than 50% of annual net sales. China is not broken out.

companies.name: UnitedHealth
companies.blurb: The largest U.S. health insurer; also owns the Optum care and pharmacy businesses.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K is focused on U.S. Medicare, Medicaid, and employer plans. China is not a disclosed market.

companies.name: Merck
companies.blurb: A drugmaker; Keytruda is its best-known cancer medicine.
companies.warNote: Sales by subsidiaries outside the U.S. were 44% of FY2025 sales. China is discussed in the filing but not broken out as a percentage.

companies.name: Bank of America
companies.blurb: A major U.S. bank for consumers, companies, and wealth-management clients.
companies.warNote: FY2025 Asia revenue, net of interest expense, was $6.0B versus $97.7B in the U.S.

companies.name: Home Depot
companies.blurb: The largest U.S. home-improvement retailer for contractors and do-it-yourself customers.
companies.warNote: Only a small share of sales is international, but the 10-K says it kept sourcing offices in China, Taiwan, Vietnam, India, Mexico, and Canada in fiscal 2025.

companies.name: GE Aerospace
companies.blurb: Builds jet engines and provides maintenance for commercial and military aircraft.
companies.warNote: Defense & Systems revenue was $6.57B in 2025, a minority of the company versus commercial engines and services. Global aviation supply and Asia sales are material, but this is not primarily a defense name.

companies.name: Intel
companies.blurb: Designs and manufactures PC and server chips; is also trying to build chips for others.
companies.warNote: Billings to China were 24% of FY2025 revenue; 70% of revenue was outside the U.S. The 10-K also discusses TSMC and Samsung as the other firms investing in leading-edge manufacturing.

companies.name: Philip Morris International
companies.blurb: Sells cigarettes and smoke-free products such as IQOS, mostly outside the U.S.
companies.warNote: The 10-K lists state-owned tobacco enterprises in China as competitors, not as a disclosed PMI revenue line. China remains largely a domestic state monopoly.

companies.name: Applied Materials
companies.blurb: Sells the machines chipmakers use to manufacture semiconductors.
companies.warNote: About 89% of FY2025 net revenue was to customers outside the U.S. Manufacturing and support are in Taiwan, China, Korea, and other Asia sites. A compiled 10-K table (Midgard/MetricsHour) puts China at about 30%; that exact share is unverified here.

companies.name: Morgan Stanley
companies.blurb: An investment bank and wealth manager (including E*TRADE and a large advisor force).
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K describes a global firm but does not break out a material China revenue share in the extract used here.

companies.name: Lam Research
companies.blurb: Sells equipment that etches and cleans chips inside semiconductor factories.
companies.warNote: FY2026 revenue mix by customer location: China 34%, Taiwan 22%, Korea 19%, Japan 9%, U.S. 7%.

companies.name: Texas Instruments
companies.blurb: Makes analog chips that go into cars, factory equipment, and electronics.
companies.warNote: China was $3.78B, or 21%, of FY2025 revenue. TI also has a site in Taipei.

companies.name: Caterpillar
companies.blurb: Makes construction, mining, and power-generation machines, plus the Cat dealer network.
companies.warNote: FY2025 external sales were $32.9B inside the U.S. and $34.7B outside (51% international). Asia/Pacific is a reported region; China is not broken out.

companies.name: RTX
companies.blurb: A major defense and aerospace contractor (Raytheon, Pratt & Whitney, Collins).
companies.warNote: A U.S. defense prime. The 10-K discusses Chinese sanctions on the Raytheon business over foreign military sales to Taiwan.

companies.name: Palo Alto Networks
companies.blurb: Sells cybersecurity software and appliances to companies and governments.
companies.warNote: Asia Pacific and Japan were $1.37B, or 12%, of FY2026 revenue ($11.5B). The 10-K says supply is concentrated in Asia and that it is monitoring China-Taiwan tensions.

companies.name: Goldman Sachs
companies.blurb: A global investment bank and asset manager serving companies, governments, and wealthy clients.
companies.warNote: The 10-K warns that a China-Taiwan conflict could hit financial markets and clients. No material China revenue share is broken out.

companies.name: Arista Networks
companies.blurb: Makes high-speed network switches used in large data centers.
companies.warNote: Asia-Pacific was 9% of FY2025 revenue ($813M of $9.01B). The 10-K cites manufacturing in Malaysia and Vietnam and political tensions between China and Taiwan.

companies.name: Thermo Fisher
companies.blurb: Sells lab equipment, scientific instruments, and research supplies to hospitals and drug companies.
companies.warNote: Asia-Pacific was $8.1B, or 18%, of FY2025 revenue ($44.6B). China is not broken out.

companies.name: Wells Fargo
companies.blurb: A large U.S. bank focused on consumers, small businesses, and commercial lending.
companies.warNote: A primarily U.S. bank. The FY2025 10-K primary document available here was incomplete, so a China percentage could not be verified.

companies.name: Netflix
companies.blurb: The leading subscription streaming service for TV shows and movies.
companies.warNote: FY2025 streaming revenue: U.S. and Canada $20.0B, EMEA $14.5B, Latin America $5.4B, Asia-Pacific $5.4B (12%) of $45.2B. The service is not generally available in China.

companies.name: Amgen
companies.blurb: A biotechnology company that makes medicines for cancer, inflammation, and other diseases.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K discusses registration requirements in China and other Asian markets but does not break out a China revenue share.

companies.name: Dell Technologies
companies.blurb: Makes PCs, servers, and storage systems for businesses and consumers.
companies.warNote: FY2026 10-K says it sells in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and other regions and points to Note 18 for non-U.S. sales. A compiled table (Midgard) puts international sales at 44%; that exact share is unverified here. PC and server supply chains are concentrated in Asia.

companies.name: CrowdStrike
companies.blurb: Sells cloud cybersecurity software (the Falcon platform) to companies worldwide.
companies.warNote: FY2026 10-K says it sells worldwide; property and equipment are concentrated in the U.S. and Germany. China is not a disclosed revenue line.

companies.name: IBM
companies.blurb: Sells business software, consulting, and hybrid-cloud services, including watsonx AI.
companies.warNote: The FY2025 Form 10-K incorporates segment and geographic tables by reference to the Annual Report to Stockholders; a China or Asia percentage could not be extracted from the filing text available here. Rating omitted.

companies.name: ConocoPhillips
companies.blurb: An oil and gas producer with large U.S. shale and LNG operations.
companies.warNote: Produces in the U.S., Norway, Canada, Australia, Malaysia, Libya, China, Qatar, and Equatorial Guinea. Asia Pacific was 4% of 2025 liquids production and 2% of natural gas.

companies.name: Linde
companies.blurb: The world's largest industrial-gases company (oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen).
companies.warNote: Operates in about 15 Asian and South Pacific countries, including China. A compiled 10-K table (Midgard) puts China at about 8%; that exact share is unverified here. Incorporated in the U.K.; included because it is in the S&P 500.

companies.name: Newmont
companies.blurb: The world's largest gold-mining company, with mines in the Americas, Australia, and Africa.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K discusses China as a factor in gold and metal demand, not as a disclosed revenue geography. Mines are in the Americas, Australia, and Africa.

companies.name: Freeport-McMoRan
companies.blurb: A major copper and gold miner (Grasberg in Indonesia, plus U.S. and South American mines).
companies.warNote: The 10-K says China is currently the largest consumer of refined copper and that U.S.-China tension can affect demand. Operations are in Indonesia, the U.S., and South America.

companies.name: NextEra Energy
companies.blurb: Florida's main electric utility, plus a large U.S. wind and solar generation business.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K is focused on Florida Power & Light and U.S. clean-energy generation. No China operations are disclosed.

companies.name: Southern Company
companies.blurb: An electric utility serving customers in the southeastern United States.
companies.warNote: A U.S. regulated utility. FY2025 10-K does not disclose China operations.

companies.name: Duke Energy
companies.blurb: An electric and gas utility serving customers in the Carolinas, Florida, and the Midwest.
companies.warNote: A U.S. regulated utility. FY2025 10-K does not disclose China operations.

companies.name: Welltower
companies.blurb: A healthcare real-estate company that owns senior-housing and medical buildings.
companies.warNote: FY2025 10-K describes U.S., U.K., and Canadian healthcare properties. China is not a disclosed market.

companies.name: Prologis
companies.blurb: The largest warehouse-and-logistics landlord, serving e-commerce and supply-chain customers.
companies.warNote: A global logistics landlord with a material Asia portfolio in addition to the Americas and Europe. A precise China percentage was not extracted from the 10-K text used here, so the Asia exposure is qualitative.

companies.name: Equinix
companies.blurb: Owns data-center campuses where companies plug their networks and cloud gear together.
companies.warNote: A global data-center operator with a disclosed Asia-Pacific footprint in addition to the Americas and EMEA. A precise China revenue share was not extracted from the 10-K text used here, so the Asia exposure is qualitative.
